title: Unit 5: Applications of Computing & Emerging Technologies

questions.question: What is the Internet of Things (IoT)?

options.A: A network of physical devices embedded with sensors, software, and connectivity to exchange data over the internet
options.B: A static cable connection between a personal computer and a printer
options.C: A closed mainframe system without network interfaces
options.D: An operating system used exclusively on supercomputers

questions.explanation: IoT refers to billions of physical objects interconnected via sensors, actuators, and IP communications to collect and exchange real-time data.

questions.question: Which lightweight messaging protocol based on the publish/subscribe model is widely adopted in resource-constrained IoT devices?

options.A: MQTT (Message Queuing Telemetry Transport)
options.B: FTP (File Transfer Protocol)
options.C: BGP (Border Gateway Protocol)
options.D: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol)

questions.explanation: MQTT is an extremely lightweight publish/subscribe messaging protocol designed for high-latency, low-bandwidth, and battery-constrained IoT devices.

questions.question: What is Cloud Computing?

options.A: The on-demand delivery of computing services (servers, storage, databases, networking, software) over the internet with pay-as-you-go pricing
options.B: Storing backup files on local magnetic tapes and CD-ROMs
options.C: Transmitting radio waves through atmospheric storm clouds
options.D: Running CPU overclocking scripts on personal laptops

questions.explanation: Cloud computing offers scalable virtualized infrastructure and applications over the internet without requiring local hardware management.

questions.question: Which cloud service delivery model provides virtualized physical computing resources such as virtual machines, storage, and networking (e.g., AWS EC2)?

options.A: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
options.B: Platform as a Service (PaaS)
options.C: Software as a Service (SaaS)
options.D: Function as a Service (FaaS)

questions.explanation: IaaS provides fundamental compute, network, and storage building blocks, leaving operating system and application management to the user.

questions.question: Which cloud computing model offers hardware and software development frameworks (like Heroku or Google App Engine) where developers focus purely on code?

options.A: Platform as a Service (PaaS)
options.B: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
options.C: Software as a Service (SaaS)
options.D: Desktop as a Service (DaaS)

questions.explanation: PaaS abstracts operating systems, runtime environments, and server hardware, allowing developers to deploy applications effortlessly.

questions.question: What is Software as a Service (SaaS)?

options.A: Delivering centrally hosted software applications over a web browser (e.g., Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Canva)
options.B: Selling software on physical DVD-ROM discs
options.C: Writing custom device drivers for motherboard graphics cards
options.D: Allocating physical hard drives in an on-premises data closet

questions.explanation: SaaS delivers ready-to-use software applications accessible to end users over the internet, managed entirely by the software vendor.

questions.question: What is a Blockchain in distributed computing?

options.A: A decentralized, distributed, and cryptographically linked digital ledger that securely records transactions across multiple peer nodes
options.B: A single centralized MySQL database managed by one system administrator
options.C: A physical chain of SATA hard drives inside a server rack
options.D: A compiler optimization technique that eliminates dead loop branches

questions.explanation: Blockchain uses cryptographic hashes and consensus protocols to maintain an immutable, tamper-evident shared ledger across distributed participants.

questions.question: How are individual blocks linked together cryptographically in a blockchain?

options.A: Each block contains the cryptographic hash of the immediately preceding block
options.B: Blocks are sorted alphabetically by author surname
options.C: Blocks share the same unencrypted IP address
options.D: Blocks are indexed by their physical hard disk sector address

questions.explanation: Every block stores the cryptographic hash of the previous block; any alteration of earlier data invalidates all subsequent block hashes.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a Consensus Mechanism (such as Proof of Work or Proof of Stake) in a blockchain network?

options.A: To ensure all decentralized nodes agree on the valid state of the ledger without trusting a central authority
options.B: To compress video files for mobile streaming
options.C: To compile Python scripts into ARM assembly code
options.D: To assign dynamic IP addresses to home Wi-Fi routers

questions.explanation: Consensus mechanisms guarantee Byzantine fault tolerance, allowing decentralized nodes to agree on transaction legitimacy without central intermediaries.

questions.question: What is an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) inspired by in computational intelligence?

options.A: The structure and functioning of biological neural networks in the human brain
options.B: The rotational dynamics of internal combustion engines
options.C: The electrical grid wiring of commercial transformers
options.D: The optical reflection of concave telescope lenses

questions.explanation: ANNs mimic biological brains using interconnected artificial nodes (neurons) organized in input, hidden, and output layers with adjustable weights.

questions.question: In an artificial neuron (Perceptron), what is the function of the Activation Function (e.g., ReLU, Sigmoid)?

options.A: To introduce non-linearity into the network, enabling it to learn complex non-linear patterns
options.B: To format floating-point numbers into JSON strings
options.C: To terminate the Python interpreter process
options.D: To allocate virtual RAM for graphics shaders

questions.explanation: Without non-linear activation functions, stacked neural layers would collapse into simple linear transformations, unable to solve complex tasks.

questions.question: Which algorithm is standardly used to train deep neural networks by calculating weight gradients backward from output loss?

options.A: Backpropagation (combined with Gradient Descent)
options.B: Dijkstra's Shortest Path
options.C: Euclidean GCD Algorithm
options.D: Huffman Coding

questions.explanation: Backpropagation computes error derivatives via the chain rule, updating layer weights backwards using gradient descent optimization.

questions.question: What distinguishes Deep Learning from traditional shallow Machine Learning algorithms?

options.A: Deep Learning employs deep neural networks with multiple hidden layers that automatically extract hierarchical feature representations
options.B: Deep Learning requires manual hand-crafted feature engineering for every input
options.C: Deep Learning cannot process unstructured data like images or audio
options.D: Deep Learning operates strictly on non-networked single-core microcontrollers

questions.explanation: Deep learning architectures automatically discover high-level representations from raw pixels or text through deep stacks of neural layers.

questions.question: What is Edge Computing?

options.A: Processing data locally near the physical source or device (on the 'edge') rather than transmitting it to a distant centralized cloud data center
options.B: Surrounding server racks with rubber safety edges to prevent physical injuries
options.C: Executing software exclusively on legacy floppy disks
options.D: Drawing borders around geometric figures in computer graphics

questions.explanation: Edge computing reduces latency and bandwidth usage by computing data directly on or near edge gateways and IoT devices.

questions.question: Why is Edge Computing critical for Autonomous Self-Driving Vehicles?

options.A: Sub-millisecond real-time decision-making for obstacle avoidance cannot tolerate the network latency of cloud transmission
options.B: Autonomous vehicles do not have computer chips installed onboard
options.C: Cloud data centers do not support GPS coordinates
options.D: Autonomous vehicles are legally barred from using cellular networks

questions.explanation: Self-driving cars must react in milliseconds to pedestrians and hazards; edge computing on onboard GPUs guarantees real-time responsiveness.

questions.question: What is a 'Smart Contract' in the Ethereum blockchain ecosystem?

options.A: A self-executing digital program stored on the blockchain that automatically runs when predetermined conditions are met
options.B: A legal contract written in physical ink and notarized by a human attorney
options.C: A patent registered with the national intellectual property office
options.D: A software agreement that locks hardware warranties upon purchase

questions.explanation: Smart contracts are autonomous programs deployed on blockchains that execute transactions deterministically without human intermediaries.

questions.question: Which neural network architecture is the premier choice for computer vision, image classification, and object detection?

options.A: Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)
options.B: Recurrent Neural Network (RNN)
options.C: Markov Decision Process
options.D: Multilayer Perceptron with linear layers only

questions.explanation: CNNs use spatial convolution kernels and pooling layers to extract translation-invariant spatial features from 2D images.

questions.question: Which architecture utilizing self-attention mechanisms has revolutionized Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Large Language Models (LLMs)?

options.A: Transformer Architecture
options.B: Restricted Boltzmann Machine
options.C: Hopfield Network
options.D: Perceptron Matrix

questions.explanation: Transformers (introduced in 'Attention Is All You Need') power modern LLMs (GPT, Gemini, Claude) through parallelized self-attention.

questions.question: What is 'Serverless Computing' (e.g., AWS Lambda, Google Cloud Functions)?

options.A: A cloud execution model where developers execute event-driven code without provisioning, managing, or maintaining server infrastructure
options.B: Running web applications entirely without electrical servers
options.C: Hosting websites on desktop personal computers via USB cables
options.D: An operating system that deletes all server software upon boot

questions.explanation: Serverless allows developers to write code functions that scale automatically in response to events, billed only for actual execution milliseconds.

questions.question: What does 'Data Immutability' mean in the context of distributed blockchain ledgers?

options.A: Once written and confirmed by consensus, transaction records cannot be retroactively altered, updated, or deleted
options.B: Data can only be written during midnight server backups
options.C: Variables cannot be displayed on computer monitors
options.D: Files must be converted into physical paper printouts

questions.explanation: Immutability ensures that committed blockchain transactions are permanent and tamper-resistant against retroactive alteration.

questions.question: Which sensor in a modern smartphone detects orientation changes and step counts by measuring proper acceleration forces?

options.A: Accelerometer
options.B: Barometer
options.C: Hygrometer
options.D: Photometer

questions.explanation: An accelerometer measures acceleration forces along 3 axes, enabling screen rotation, step counting, and shake gesture recognition.

questions.question: What is the primary role of an 'Actuator' in a smart IoT system?

options.A: A component that converts electrical control signals into physical motion or action (e.g., opening a smart valve, turning on a motor)
options.B: A sensor that measures environmental temperature
options.C: A cryptographic key generator for SSH logins
options.D: A database index for rapid binary search

questions.explanation: While sensors detect physical stimuli, actuators perform physical actions (e.g., solenoids, relays, motors) in response to controller commands.

questions.question: What is a 'Digital Twin' in modern industrial computing and IoT?

options.A: A real-time virtual simulation model of a physical object, machine, or system updated via live sensor telemetry
options.B: A duplicate USB backup stick stored in a fireproof safe
options.C: Two programmers writing code on identical keyboards
options.D: A mirrored RAID hard drive setup on a desktop PC

questions.explanation: A digital twin bridges physical and virtual worlds, simulating performance, monitoring health, and predicting maintenance needs of industrial assets.

questions.question: Which cloud computing deployment model combines private on-premises infrastructure with public cloud services, allowing data and apps to be shared between them?

options.A: Hybrid Cloud
options.B: Community Cloud
options.C: Single-tenant Bare Metal
options.D: Localhost LAN

questions.explanation: Hybrid clouds blend private on-premises data centers with public clouds, giving businesses greater flexibility and data sovereignty compliance.

questions.question: What is 'Fog Computing' in relation to cloud and edge paradigms?

options.A: An intermediate decentralized layer between edge devices and centralized cloud data centers (e.g., local routers, base stations)
options.B: A server cooling technique utilizing aerosolized moisture
options.C: An optical network cable designed for humid tropical regions
options.D: A data scrambling algorithm used by malware authors

questions.explanation: Fog computing extends the cloud closer to edge devices, providing local compute, storage, and networking on local gateways.

questions.question: What is 'Zero Trust' architecture in modern enterprise cloud security?

options.A: A security model that requires strict identity verification for every person and device attempting to access resources, regardless of network perimeter
options.B: A policy that prohibits employees from using computers at work
options.C: An algorithm that deletes all database passwords upon creation
options.D: A firewall that blocks all outgoing HTTP requests unconditionally

questions.explanation: Zero Trust operates on the principle 'never trust, always verify', continuously authenticating and validating identity and device posture.

questions.question: Which technology allows multiple independent virtual operating system instances to run simultaneously on a single physical host server?

options.A: Virtualization (via Hypervisors)
options.B: Thread Paging
options.C: Bus Snooping
options.D: BIOS Flashing

questions.explanation: Virtualization uses a hypervisor (Type 1 or Type 2) to abstract physical hardware into isolated virtual machines (VMs).

questions.question: What is the primary difference between a Docker Container and a Virtual Machine (VM)?

options.A: Containers share the host OS kernel and are lightweight, whereas VMs package a complete guest OS on top of a hypervisor
options.B: Containers require dedicated physical CPUs for each application
options.C: VMs do not support networking or persistent disk storage
options.D: Containers can only run Python scripts and not compiled code

questions.explanation: Containers virtualize at the OS level (sharing the host kernel), making them spin up in seconds with megabytes rather than gigabytes of overhead.

questions.question: What is Computer Vision (CV)?

options.A: An AI field enabling computers to derive meaningful information from digital images, videos, and visual inputs
options.B: An optical treatment designed to cure eye strain caused by monitors
options.C: A hardware cable transmitting video signals from GPU to monitor
options.D: A camera filter that inverts screen colors

questions.explanation: Computer Vision uses deep learning to enable machines to interpret visual inputs (facial recognition, autonomous navigation, medical MRI scans).

questions.question: What is Natural Language Processing (NLP)?

options.A: The branch of artificial intelligence that gives computers the ability to understand, generate, and manipulate human language
options.B: An organic programming language compiled without electronics
options.C: A speech pathology therapy for computer programmers
options.D: A compression algorithm for English text files only

questions.explanation: NLP combines computational linguistics with machine learning to process human speech and text (sentiment analysis, translation, chatbots).

questions.question: In blockchain, what is the '51% Attack' threat?

options.A: When a single entity gains majority control of the network's mining hashrate, enabling double-spending and transaction blockage
options.B: When a hard drive reaches 51% storage capacity and corrupts files
options.C: When a router drops 51% of UDP broadcast packets
options.D: When an e-commerce website discounts products by more than half

questions.explanation: If a miner or cartel controls >50% of the hashing power, they can reorganize blocks, prevent confirmations, and double-spend cryptocurrency.

questions.question: Which protocol enables smart home IoT devices from different manufacturers to communicate securely across a unified local mesh standard?

options.A: Matter (over Thread and Wi-Fi)
options.B: Telnet
options.C: POP3
options.D: X11 Display Protocol

questions.explanation: Matter is the unified royalty-free smart home connectivity standard supported by Apple, Google, and Amazon to ensure device interoperability.

questions.question: What is the primary objective of Reinforcement Learning (RL) in artificial intelligence?

options.A: Training an autonomous agent to take actions in an environment to maximize cumulative reward through trial and error
options.B: Sorting database tables into ascending order
options.C: Scanning files for malicious macro virus signatures
options.D: Compressing images with lossy JPEG algorithms

questions.explanation: RL trains agents (e.g., AlphaGo, robotic arms) by rewarding desirable behaviors and penalizing mistakes in dynamic environments.

questions.question: What does 'SLA' stand for in commercial cloud provider contracts?

options.A: Service Level Agreement
options.B: System Logic Architecture
options.C: Standard Linux Automation
options.D: Software Licensing Authentication

questions.explanation: An SLA guarantees uptime metrics (e.g., 99.99% availability) and outlines penalties or credits if the provider experiences outages.

questions.question: How does Quantum Computing fundamentally differ from classical digital computing?

options.A: It utilizes quantum bits (Qubits) that can exist in superpositions of 0 and 1 simultaneously, enabling exponential parallelism for specific problems
options.B: It runs standard Windows executable files at higher clock speeds
options.C: It eliminates the need for computer cooling and electricity
options.D: It replaces microchips with mechanical wooden gears

questions.explanation: Qubits leverage quantum superposition and entanglement, solving complex molecular modeling and cryptographic factorizations exponentially faster.
